The core value of traditional programming languages lies in their precision—they can describe computational processes without ambiguity. But when AI can understand vague natural language and convert it into precise code, the direct value of this precision shifts from humans to the collaborative chain between humans and AI. In other words, programming languages are no longer a bridge between humans and computers, but a contract between humans and AI—you need them to tell AI what you want, and to verify that what AI gives you is indeed what you wanted.
